career.organization: State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company
career.title: President

background_rationale: A CPA who rose through State Farm's securities, planning, financial operations and underwriting roles and served eight years as CFO and treasurer before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: State Farm Mutual declared a $5 billion dividend for auto policyholders, the largest in company history, averaging about $100 per insured vehicle, following rate cuts in 40 states.
Farney described a "Human + Digital" strategy including an OpenAI partnership to speed claims and improve underwriting, saying State Farm wants the right combination of people and technology.

Discussing California, where State Farm paid over $5.7 billion in wildfire claims and raised homeowner rates, Farney said its California homeowners company was worth far less than its $4 billion value in 2017.

personal_story.hook: Jon Farney joined State Farm as an intern in his Illinois hometown in 1993; 31 years later he became its CEO.
personal_story.summary: Farney is a native of Bloomington-Normal, Illinois, home to State Farm's headquarters. He earned an accounting degree from Illinois State University in 1993 and joined State Farm that year as an intern. He spent his entire career at the company, working through securities, planning, financial operations and underwriting roles, and became a CPA along the way. After eight years as CFO, he became president in January 2024 and CEO that June. Little else about his early life has been published.
